x: In the Southern Counties Track '7' both Bob Picton and Brian Ward broke 60 Minutes to win their '7' in the hour badges. Ray Hall is on the trail back to fitness again, giving Carl Lawton a close shave in the SCAAA six at Battersea the other week.
Dave Mayo, Carl Lawton, Bernard Capener and Brian Ward gave Belgrave a magnificent start to 1968 by defeating strong opposition from Trowbridge and winning the Garnet Cup by just two points.

Carl Lawton had a stylish win in the 2 miles walk after a fast start by Brian Ward that suggested an upset was due. Several of our leading walkers were unable to be present due to a clash of dates with the Leicester '20'.

Our lads all excelled themselves in this first track race, Len Duquemin and John Moullin achieving first class standard and therefore their Club Honours Badges, Brian Ward and Bob Picton breaking the hour.
With everyone giving of his best it is difficult to single out individual performances but it says much for the future to see Carl Lawton and Brian Ward, both only 20, in such forward positions.

Support from other Belgravians was fantastic, Captain Ray Hall, Charlie MacLennan, Carl Lawton, Brian Ward, Johnny Morris, Steve Brown, The Wilson brothers as well as many others all played a part on this hot day.

Carl Lawton led the boys home followed by Brian Ward with newcomer Paul Duckett breathing down his neck only ½ a minute down. Paul still has three years to go as a junior and on his present form there will be few to beat him in a year or two.

True Bobby Barnes is not yet back to the form (or shape!) of a year ago and it is some time since we have seen or heard Dave Mayo but Carl Lawton and Brian Ward are both showing steady improvement and Gerry Cameron is also going well.

Andy Hinchcliff recorded a good 27.13 in the Youth 3 Miles and in the 6 miles Brian Ward finished sixth with some strong walking. The 10,000 metres was held on the track which was not in much of a state for fast walking.
Brian Ward, Gerry Cameron and Bob Picton all looked to be on the trail again and up north Dave King and Paul Duckett are sure to be slipping in some crafty sessions.

However on October 19th, at Manchester, Carl Lawton, Brian Ward and Paul Duckett filled fourth team position. The winter season began well for Belgrave with Len Duquemin and the club taking top honours in the Highgate Open Seven.
Barry Ingarfield and Brian Ward have also come to the fore and Pat Duncan is now busy trying to convince Dave King that he is needed for the longer ones.
Pat Duncan and Brian Ward both walked steady races but Barry Ingarfield was unhappy although he hung on determindly to close in the 8 to retain the Nijmegan Shield.
Pat Duncan is at last coming through a bit although both Brian Ward and Dave King look like catching him ( some hope !) and its good to see Dave Debondi back in the thick of it once more.

Bob Coates fell foul of the judges but Brian Ward and Pat Duncan were close at hand to ensure a comfortable victory for the team. Brian's 4.54.23 was an encouraging sign for the future even if the ever crafty Pat sneaked past in the last lap.
Carl Lawton is 27th over 3,000m., 23rd over 10,000 and 22nd over 20,000. Len Duquemin fills 28th place at 20,000m., while in the 50,000, John Moullin is 11th, Pat Duncan 16th and Brian Ward 17th
In the Metropolitan Police '10' Mile championship Brian Ward finished 4th in 86:54 and Doug Fotheringham 8th in 89:29. It appears that Charles MacLennan did not finish, the question is DID HE START ?
